newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's says unsure of GMG Brands plans.
newsitem.headline: Foster's says unsure of GMG Brands plans.

text.p: Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Thursday it did not know how the GMG Brands group would view their jointly owned British pub business.

Grand Metropolitan Plc, an equal partner with Foster's in the Inntrepreneur Pub Co Ltd, plans to merge with brewer Guinness Plc to become GMG Brands, raising queries over the merged group's commitment to the pub chain.
Foster's chairman John Ralph told Reuters he could not speculate on how GMG would view the business.

"Whether they would look at it differently in terms of their objectives and strategies as an enlarged group, compared with where GrandMet was before, is something I'm not in a position to speculate about," he told Reuters.
But he added there was no immediate significance to the Inntrepreneur business from the merger.
Foster's has first right of refusal on GMG's 50 percent stake in Inntrepreneur, and vice versa, but Ralph said his board had not considered the prospect of this opportunity emerging.
"We would have to have a look at that at the time," he said.
Inntrepreneur owns about 2,900 pubs and has property valued at 950 million pounds in GrandMet's 1996 accounts.
Inntrepreneur chief executive Mike Foster has raised the possibility of a share market float for the company, but said this would be some way off.
British analysts have valued the Inntrepreneur group at about 800 million pounds, or A$1.68 billion.
Foster's valued its half share of Inntrepreneur at A$529.2 million on September 30 last year, before accounting for its share of the British company's accumulated losses.
